CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” audit round 1, commit d536182
(branch sprint-8-duty-to-accommodate-intake), clean tree. Sprint file re-read
fresh in full immediately before this verdict, including the pre-review
adjustments, Chang's wording block, and requirements 11-22.

The core of this sprint is right, and the parts most likely to go wrong did not.
Answers are closed unions in lib/types.ts with no boolean anywhere near them.
The requirement 18 mapping is implemented exactly, including the subtle case:
requestStatus "not-sure" returns insufficient-information and is checked BEFORE
the !== "denied" branch, so an unknown request status can never fall through to
not-applicable. yesNoStatus has no not-applicable branch at all, so
alternatives-explored and analysis-documented cannot structurally return it.
The escalation trigger is narrowed to not-done or insufficient-information per
requirement 20, so an employer with nothing denied is no longer told to request
a functional abilities form. Every artefact listed in requirement 14 is gone â€”
the eslint-disable, the function-level "all three items are currently
insufficient-information" comment, and all three per-item comments. The
Sprint 5 requirement 16 limitation test is deleted outright, not weakened.
All 16 option labels and all four legends and the Q2 helper text match
requirement 16 character for character. Step stays 1 | 2 | 3 and the "of 3"
label is unchanged. buildProsePayload still takes only an AnalysisResult and no
dutyToAccommodate field appears anywhere in the prose path. lib/types.ts changes
are bounded to requirement 21. Vitest 60/60, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint exit 0.

REQUIRED BEFORE SHIP:

1. [MEDIUM] aria-invalid is missing on all four new questions â€” requirement 8.

   Requirement 8 names three attributes for the new questions specifically:
   role="alert", aria-describedby, and aria-invalid. The first two are present â€”
   role="alert" on the shared error at components/IntakeFlow.tsx:783,
   aria-describedby wired through describedById at :625. aria-invalid appears
   nowhere on the new questions.

   This is an omission against an explicit requirement, not an absent house
   convention: the same file already sets aria-invalid on the tenure input
   (:443) and on every narrative textarea (:584). The new questions were held to
   a lower bar than the fields beside them.

   On the fix: aria-invalid on the <fieldset> alone is weak, since assistive
   technology generally announces validity on the focusable control rather than
   on a grouping element. Either set it on each radio input, or give the group
   role="radiogroup" and set it there. Worth doing properly â€” this is a tool
   whose users are employers making a legal decision, and the error being
   announced is the one telling them the form is incomplete.

2. [MEDIUM] Two required Vitest cases were not implemented, and nothing says so.

   Requirement 10 asks for "the conditional question not appearing when no
   denial is indicated". Requirement 22 asks for "Q2 and Q3 rendering for every
   Q0 answer, including no request has been made". Neither exists.

   Both are assertions about rendering, and this repo has no capability to make
   them: no *.test.tsx anywhere, no @testing-library, no jsdom or happy-dom in
   package.json. The nearest existing tests â€” "returns not-applicable when no
   request was ever denied" and the yes/no/not-sure sweep â€” exercise the rules
   consequence of those answers, not the rendering behaviour, so they do not
   substitute for what was asked.

   I confirmed the behaviour itself by reading the JSX, and it is correct: Q1
   alone is wrapped in {requestStatus === "denied" && ...} at :750, and Q2 and
   Q3 render unconditionally at :761 and :771. So the acceptance criteria
   phrased as "QA1 confirms..." are satisfied. The requirements asking for
   Vitest cases are not.

   The resolution is not obviously Dev Team's to pick. Covering these means
   adding @testing-library/react and a DOM environment, and CLAUDE.md's testing
   section specifies unit tests on logic with no in-repo end-to-end tests â€”
   whether that admits component render tests is a standards question for
   Master Controller. What is squarely Dev Team's is that the gap was left
   silent: no note in the commit, no flag, nothing. A requirement that cannot be
   met as written gets raised, not skipped.

3. [LOW] The intake summary shows the user raw union values.

   components/IntakeFlow.tsx:857, :866, :875 and :881 render requestStatus,
   documentationTiming, alternativesExplored and writtenRecord directly, so the
   confirmation screen reads "no-request", "before-decision", "not-sure". The
   human labels already exist forty lines away in REQUEST_STATUS_OPTIONS and its
   three siblings; look the label up rather than printing the slug.

   Not a regression â€” the same summary already prints employmentStatus and
   concerns raw, from Sprint 3. Raising it because this sprint had four
   questions' wording reviewed by Chang for leading and ambiguous phrasing, and
   then echoes the answers back as enum slugs. If the wording matters enough for
   a legal review, it matters on the way back out.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER â€” not a defect in this diff, and it will block gate 2:

4. Three of Sprint 8's five GroundTruth criteria are untestable as written, and
   it is the same defect this sprint file cites twice as a lesson already
   learned.

   They ask GroundTruth to complete intake and confirm "the checklist reports
   done on those items", "the checklist reports the gap, and that an escalation
   trigger appears", and "the checklist reports missing information and never
   asserts the employer failed a step". All three require a rendered checklist.

   Nothing renders one. Out of Scope says rendering stays with Sprint 6, and
   Dependencies says Sprint 8 blocks Sprint 6, so Sprint 6 has not run. I
   verified this rather than assuming it: no file under app/ or components/
   calls analyzeSituation, analyzeAndPhrase, or buildProceduralChecklist, and
   the only consumer of a checklist item's status anywhere in the codebase is
   escalation-trigger-rules.ts.

   This is precisely the shape CLAUDE.md's gate-2 section describes, and the
   shape this sprint file invokes when explaining why Sprint 5's criteria were
   moved to Sprint 6. Left as written it deadlocks gate 2 the way Sprint 1
   requirement 8 deadlocked gate 1. Either move those three criteria to Sprint
   6, or state that Sprint 8 ships behind Sprint 6 and adjust the dependency.
   Gate 2's honest scope here is non-regression on the Sprint 3 flow plus the
   new questions being present, keyboard-navigable, and validating â€” which the
   remaining two criteria already cover.

STANDING LIMIT: I verified the answer unions, the mapping, the conditional
logic, and that the wording matches what Chang approved. I cannot verify the
questions are the right questions to ask â€” whether "was documentation requested
before the denial" is the correct legal test, or whether these four answers
actually establish duty-to-accommodate compliance. That is law, not code. The
sprint's Dependencies section records Chang's wording review as approved, and
the deferred item (whether Q2 should ask if alternatives were discussed with the
employee rather than merely considered) is correctly left unimplemented per that
same note.

Re-audit required. Finding 2 needs a Master Controller call on component tests
before Dev Team can close it. Do not run /sprint-dev-done on this verdict.
